title: Orienting Your CDS Caregiver: The 8 Topics Missouri Requires
short_title: Orienting your CDS caregiver: the 8 topics
description: In Missouri's Consumer Directed Services (CDS) program, the person getting care is the employer, and Missouri asks every employer to orient their new caregiver on eight topics. Here are all eight: the plan of care, how you like things done, recording time honestly, confidentiality, abuse and neglect, emergencies, infection control, and what to do when it isn't working.
end: Get the printable checklist at caringcds.com.

parts.head: Orienting your CDS caregiver: the 8 topics
parts.sub: What Missouri asks every CDS employer to cover
parts.text: In Missouri's CDS program, you're the employer. And Missouri asks every employer to orient their new caregiver on eight topics before they start. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS. Here are all eight.

parts.head: One honest conversation
parts.sub: With a checklist. We help you prepare.
parts.text: It sounds formal. In practice, it's one honest conversation with a checklist. You can do it in one sitting, or across the first week. We help you prepare for it when you enroll.

parts.head: The tasks in the plan of care
parts.sub: What they're paid to do, and what's not part of it
parts.text: One: the tasks in the plan of care. Walk through what the state approved, task by task, so your caregiver knows what they're paid to do, and what isn't part of the job.

parts.head: How you like things done
parts.text: Two: how you like things done. Your morning routine, how you like to be helped up, where the good mugs are, whether you want conversation or quiet. Say it out loud once.

parts.head: Recording time honestly
parts.sub: Clock in and out as it happens
parts.text: Three: recording time honestly. Clock in when the shift starts, and out when it ends. Never early, and never after the fact. And explain that you approve the hours each week.

parts.head: Confidentiality
parts.sub: Health, home and finances stay private. No photos.
parts.text: Four: confidentiality. Your health, your household, and your finances stay in your home. That includes social media: no photos of you, your home, or your paperwork.

parts.head: Abuse and neglect
parts.sub: Share the hotline. Reporting is a duty.
parts.text: Five: recognizing and reporting abuse or neglect. Missouri requires this conversation. Share the hotline number, and make clear that reporting a concern is a duty, not a betrayal.

parts.head: Emergencies, and who to call
parts.sub: Write down the order of calls
parts.text: Six: emergencies, and who to call. A fire, a fall, a medical emergency, or no answer at the door. Write down the order of calls, and keep the list where you can both find it fast.

parts.head: Infection control and safe handling
parts.sub: Handwashing, gloves, safe transfers, clear walkways
parts.text: Seven: infection control and safe handling. Handwashing, gloves, safe lifting and transferring, and clear walkways. It's basic, and it's why most avoidable injuries don't happen.

parts.head: When it isn't working
parts.sub: You set the standard. Agree how to raise a problem.
parts.text: Eight: what to do when it isn't working. You're the employer, so you set the standard, and you can end the arrangement. Agree now how you'll raise a problem, and tell your caregiver they can raise one, too.

parts.head: Do it anyway
parts.sub: Twenty minutes now saves arguments later
parts.text: If your caregiver is your daughter or your neighbor, this can feel awfully formal. Do it anyway. The families who skip it are the ones arguing in month three about whether laundry was ever part of the deal.

parts.head: The Attendant Orientation, online
parts.sub: Your caregiver learns the program rules too
parts.text: Your caregiver also takes the free Attendant Orientation online, which covers the program rules from their side. Your conversation covers your home and your preferences, which nobody else can teach.
There's a printable checklist at caringcds.com. Questions? Call us at 417-218-2888. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS. Thanks for watching.
